name: Our Lady Aparecida
place: Paraíba do Sul River, Guaratinguetá, São Paulo, Brazil
visionaries: The fishermen João Alves, Felipe Pedroso and Domingos Garcia
summary: Not an apparition: the National Shrine records that in October 1717 three fishermen drew from the Paraíba River a small image of Our Lady of the Conception, first the body and then the head, followed by an abundant catch. The devotion grew around that image.
recognition: The cult was approved on 5 May 1743 by the Bishop of Rio de Janeiro, Dom Frei João da Cruz. By a decree of 16 July 1930, Pius XI made Our Lady of the Conception Aparecida Patroness of Brazil, proclaimed on 31 May 1931.
fonte: Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, História de Nossa Senhora Aparecida: https://www.a12.com/santuario/historia-de-nossa-senhora-aparecida-1717; decreto de 1930: https://www.a12.com/academia/artigos/por-que-nossa-senhora-aparecida-e-padroeira-do-brasil

name: Our Lady of Lourdes
summary: The Sanctuary of Lourdes records eighteen apparitions to Bernadette Soubirous at the Grotto of Massabielle, beginning on 11 February 1858.
recognition: On 18 January 1862, Mgr Laurence, Bishop of Tarbes, judged in a pastoral mandate that the Immaculate truly appeared to Bernadette, eighteen times, and that the faithful are justified in believing it; he authorized public worship and asked for a sanctuary to be built. The judgement rested on a commission of inquiry opened in 1858.
fonte: Sanctuaire Notre-Dame de Lourdes, The recognition of the Lourdes Apparitions: https://www.lourdes-france.com/en/the-recognition-of-the-lourdes-apparitions/

name: Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal
place: Chapel of the Daughters of Charity, Rue du Bac, Paris, France
summary: The Rue du Bac chapel records three apparitions to Catherine Labouré, a novice of the Daughters of Charity, on 18 July, 27 November and in December 1830. On 27 November, Mary asked for a medal to be struck with the invocation "O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee".
recognition: The Archbishop of Paris, Mgr de Quélen, authorized the first medals, struck in June 1832. The canonical inquiry opened in 1835 remained incomplete, because Catherine kept her anonymity; the chapel records that Leo XIII approved the Mass of the feast in 1894 and that Pius XII canonized her in 1947, after a process that included an inquiry into the apparitions.
fonte: Chapelle Notre-Dame de la Médaille Miraculeuse, 27 novembre 1830: https://www.chapellenotredamedelamedaillemiraculeuse.com/apparitions-et-medaille/27-novembre-1830/; Histoire de la Médaille: https://www.chapellenotredamedelamedaillemiraculeuse.com/apparitions-et-medaille/medaille-miraculeuse/histoire-de-la-medaille/
